title: "Semantic Search"
description: "A search approach that retrieves items based on meaning or intent rather than only exact word overlap."
term: "Semantic Search"
letter: "S"
category: "Retrieval"
difficulty: "Intermediate"
---

## Simple explanation

Semantic search tries to find results that mean something similar to a
query, even when they use different words. A search for “how to fix a
leaking tap” might find a guide titled “repairing a dripping faucet.”

## Technical explanation

Semantic retrieval commonly encodes queries and documents into vector
representations and searches by similarity. Other approaches use learned
ranking models or language understanding. Quality depends on the embedding
model, domain, index, query processing, and evaluation judgments.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Semantic search can improve discovery when queries and documents use
different terminology. It is often used in RAG and enterprise search, but
exact lexical matching remains valuable for names, identifiers, and precise
terms.

## How it works

Documents are encoded and indexed. At query time the system encodes the
query, retrieves semantically nearby candidates, applies filters or
reranking, and returns results. Hybrid systems combine this with keyword
retrieval to handle both meaning and exact matches.

## Practical example

A help center can embed each article and retrieve candidates for a
paraphrased user question. Evaluate recall and ranking using representative
queries, including exact product codes and domain-specific terminology.

## Common misconceptions

- Semantic search does not guarantee factual or relevant results; vector
  similarity is only a proxy.
- It does not make keyword search obsolete; hybrid retrieval often handles
  more query types effectively.
